title: West Coast July
meta_desc: Explore NZ's West Coast with kids in July. Discover glaciers, pancake rocks, and wild beaches. Plan your family trip with our guide, including weather, events.
intro: The West Coast of New Zealand is a fantastic destination for families, even in the winter month of July. With its stunning natural beauty, including glaciers, pancake rocks, and wild beaches, there's plenty to see and do. In this guide, we'll help you plan your family trip to the West Coast in July, including what to expect from the weather, what's on, and some practical tips for visiting with kids.

sections.heading: Weather in July
sections.body:
July is winter on the West Coast, and you can expect cooler temperatures, ranging from 5-12°C. It's also one of the wettest months, with an average of 12 rainy days. However, the rainforests and glaciers are at their most lush and beautiful, making it a great time to visit.

Make sure to pack warm and waterproof clothing, including coats, gloves, and hats. The coastal winds can be strong, so it's a good idea to bring a windbreaker or umbrella.

sections.heading: What's On in July
sections.body:
There are several events and festivals happening on the West Coast in July, including the Hokitika Winter Festival. This festival features live music, food stalls, and a fireworks display.

The West Coast is also home to several museums and galleries, which are great places to visit on a rainy day. The Hokitika Museum and the Coaltown Museum are both worth a visit.

sections.heading: Best Activities for Families
sections.body:
Some of the best activities for families on the West Coast include visiting the Punakaiki Pancake Rocks and Blowholes, taking a walk on the Franz Josef Glacier, and exploring the Hokitika Gorge.

The Punakaiki Pancake Rocks are a must-see, with their unique layered rock formations and stunning coastal views. The Franz Josef Glacier is also a great place to visit, with its beautiful ice formations and scenic walks.
list: Franz Josef Glacier (free walk to terminal face)

sections.heading: Practical Tips for Families
sections.body: Here are some practical tips for families visiting the West Coast in July:
list: Book your accommodation and activities ahead of time, especially during school holidays
Pack warm and waterproof clothing, including coats, gloves, and hats
Bring a windbreaker or umbrella to protect against coastal winds
Take advantage of free activities, such as visiting the Punakaiki Pancake Rocks and walking on the Franz Josef Glacier
Consider visiting during the week to avoid crowds

sections.heading: Crowd Levels and Booking Ahead
sections.body:
Crowd levels on the West Coast in July are generally lower than during the peak summer months, but it's still a good idea to book your accommodation and activities ahead of time, especially during school holidays.

Some popular activities, such as guided glacier walks and helicopter tours, may require booking several weeks in advance. However, many free activities, such as visiting the Punakaiki Pancake Rocks and walking on the Franz Josef Glacier, do not require booking ahead.
